title: Will anyone pay for the flood barrier?

vars: C<100 ? "built by one neighbour paying alone" : (C<200 ? "not built, although it is worth building" : "not built (not worth building)")

predict.q: Ana and Ben each value a flood barrier at **100**; neither can be left out. It costs **150**. If both pay, they split the cost (75 each). If one pays, that person pays all 150. Each decides alone. What happens?

options.fb: Both paying gives 25 each, but if Ben pays, Ana does better by not paying (100). Paying together is not stable.

options.s: One pays 150 and the other free rides
options.fb: Paying alone gives −50, worse than 0. At this cost nobody pays alone.

options.s: Neither pays, and the barrier is not built
options.fb: Whatever the other does, not paying is better for each (100 > 25 and 0 > −50): the barrier is not built.

options.s: It is built, because 200 is more than 150
options.fb: 200 > 150 shows the barrier is worth building, but no one decides for the pair. Each compares their own payoffs.

task: Move the cost slider from 20 to 300 and watch each neighbor's best choice in the payoff grid.

target.do: Move the cost slider, then press Check.

takeaway: Below a cost of 100 one neighbor may pay alone; between 100 and 200 a barrier worth building is not built.
explore: Ticks mark each neighbor's best reply; the yellow cell is where neither wants to change.
alt: Will anyone pay for the flood barrier?

inv: C<100 ? has(R2,'alone') : (C<200 ? has(R2,'worth building') : has(R2,'not worth'))
